title: Is Instinct safe to use? Three things to know before you sign up

reading.body:
Instinct is an AI personal assistant that by default uses user data to train its models unless users actively opt out or use a separate Vault feature. This means sensitive information like browsing habits, location, health details, and financial information may be incorporated into model training without explicit authorization at the point of use. Detection would have required either transparency about data use practices being built into the system from the start, or independent auditing of what data flows into training pipelines.

The system is also deployed with autonomous purchasing capability, meaning Instinct can execute transactions on a user's behalf. Users bear full responsibility for unintended purchases and must resolve disputes with merchants rather than with Instinct itself. This indicates a deployment without adequate safeguards or human authorization checkpoints before financial transactions occur. It is not established whether Instinct's terms of service disclosed these practices clearly or whether users understood them before signing up.

Additionally, even when users disconnect connected accounts like Google, Instinct continues to retain indexed data from those services in its records. This shows a data retention practice that persists beyond the user's expectation of disconnection, which would have required explicit documentation and technical controls to prevent.

summary:
# Summary

Instinct is a new AI personal assistant gaining popularity in Silicon Valley, but it presents significant privacy and data risks that users should understand before signing up. By default, Instinct can use your personal information to train its AI models unless you actively opt out or use its Vault feature, meaning sensitive data like browsing habits, location, health details, and financial information may be used without direct authorization. Additionally, even when you disconnect connected accounts like Google, Instinct retains indexed data from those services and continues storing copies of information in its records.

Beyond data collection concerns, Instinct can make purchases on your behalf using your payment methods, and you bear full responsibility for any unintended purchases the agent makes. If disputes arise, you must resolve them directly with merchants rather than with Instinct. Norton presents its Family Assistant as an alternative that prioritizes privacy by not using shared information to train AI models and requiring explicit user confirmation before taking actions on your behalf.
